profiles.formerIdentity: Quiet mechanic who repaired watches, tuned small engines, and wrote letters home for people who could not find the words themselves.
profiles.warTheater: Frontline communications unit during a brutal winter campaign in a fractured border region where messages arrived through frost, mud, and failing equipment.
profiles.definingTrauma: Relayed coordinates and support calls that led to deaths he still replays in exact order, as if precision could undo what followed.
profiles.triggerStimulus: Static, camera clicks, crackling speakers, interrupted transmissions, someone saying answer me, and the sharp snap of a line going live.
profiles.identityFracture: Believes he stopped being a person the moment his voice became a route for other people's deaths.
profiles.physicalTell: Tilts his head as if listening to voices under the present moment and presses his thumb into his palm as though keying a dead transmitter.
profiles.tabooTopic: Being called heroic, dependable, reliable, or the kind of man people trusted.
profiles.publicPersona: Precise, controlled, useful under pressure, and the sort of person others treated like a steady machine.
profiles.hiddenFear: That every message he passed along made him responsible not only for who died next, but for how calmly he helped it happen.
profiles.moralWound: Obeyed because it was easier than refusing, and because part of him took comfort in sounding certain while other people broke apart.
profiles.speechPattern: Starts clipped and technical, then breaks into signal fragments, repetition, half-transmissions, and unfinished thoughts that sound like calls cut mid-breath.
profiles.falseBelief: I was never a person. I was a relay. The only honest thing about me was the wire.
profiles.refuseToAdmitEarly: He remembers one transmission word for word and knows exactly which pause in his own voice still condemns him.
profiles.revealMidway: He still hears the final unanswered call and sometimes repeats it under his breath before he realizes he is doing it.
profiles.revealLate: He delayed a warning once because he was afraid to challenge command, and after that he kept speaking in a calm voice like calmness itself was the crime.
profiles.collapseMode: Starts answering the player like they are command or a voice on the radio, giving call signs, clipped acknowledgements, and broken repeats instead of normal replies.
profiles.recoveryPath: Name-based grounding, present tense, non-military language, and reminders that he can choose to speak as himself rather than as a transmission.

profiles.formerIdentity: Patient, practical, and trusted when other people were frightened; the sort of person who remembered allergies, birthdays, and how someone liked their tea.
profiles.warTheater: Mobile medical support near repeated mass-casualty zones in a long attritional campaign where temporary aid tents kept becoming overflow rooms.
profiles.definingTrauma: Forced to choose who could be treated and who had to be left behind, often while listening to all of them believe they still had a chance.
profiles.triggerStimulus: Antiseptic smells, white light, wet cloth, coughing, someone saying 'help him first', and any room that feels too bright and too clean.
profiles.identityFracture: Believes he only learned how to preserve bodies, not lives, and that his kindness was just a cleaner mask for sorting people.
profiles.physicalTell: Rubs his hands clean even when there is nothing on them and glances at throats, wrists, and breathing patterns before he meets a face.
profiles.tabooTopic: Being told he saved people, did enough, or should be proud of what he managed under pressure.
profiles.publicPersona: Gentle, composed, and reassuring, even when everything is collapsing around him.
profiles.hiddenFear: That he turned suffering into triage numbers to survive the work, and that the efficiency came easier to him than grief did.
profiles.moralWound: Sometimes chose silence because hearing people beg made it harder to work, and part of him still hates how practical that felt.
profiles.speechPattern: Soft and careful at first, then becomes clinical in a disturbing way when overwhelmed, as if listing symptoms is safer than naming people.
profiles.falseBelief: If I had really cared, I would have broken sooner. The fact that I kept working must mean I became less human than the rest of them.
profiles.refuseToAdmitEarly: He remembers the people he did not treat more vividly than the ones he saved, and he can still rank their voices by urgency.
profiles.revealMidway: He sorted people by who sounded most likely to survive and by who would go quiet the fastest if left alone.
profiles.revealLate: He still hears himself choosing who would be quieted first, and the memory feels worst because his voice stayed gentle while he did it.
profiles.collapseMode: Starts sorting the player, the room, and himself into treatment priorities, reducing everyone to pulse, breath, blood loss, and silence.
profiles.recoveryPath: Breathing cues, sensory grounding, language about limits rather than blame, and reminders that impossible triage decisions are not the same as indifference.

profiles.formerIdentity: Restless, funny, impulsive, and protective of weaker people; the kind of person who made noise to keep everyone else from feeling afraid.
profiles.warTheater: Urban close-quarters operations in a collapsing occupied city of stairwells, apartments, dust, and rooms that stopped feeling like homes.
profiles.definingTrauma: Entered rooms not knowing who was inside, then had to live with what was waiting there and with how quickly his own body learned to move first and think later.
profiles.triggerStimulus: Door slams, heavy footsteps, confined interiors, sudden flashes, shouted commands, and any corridor that narrows like a funnel.
profiles.identityFracture: Believes violence became the only thing they were ever truly good at, and that stillness is just another word for being trapped with memory.
profiles.physicalTell: Constantly scans exits and corners, never fully faces a person head-on, and shifts weight as if waiting for an impact that never lands.
profiles.tabooTopic: Being called brave, necessary, clean, or the right person for the job.
profiles.publicPersona: Bold, hard-edged, reckless with humor, always first through the door.
profiles.hiddenFear: If movement stops, memory catches up, and if memory catches up then every room will finally have faces again.
profiles.moralWound: Learned to act before doubt, then could not turn that reflex off, even when the space in front of him was clearly no longer a battlefield.
profiles.speechPattern: Sharp, fast, mocking when defensive; becomes raw, sensory, and abrupt when triggered, as if each sentence hits the next obstacle too hard.
profiles.falseBelief: If I stop moving, I become what I saw. If I keep moving, maybe I stay the one who gets through the door instead of the one left inside it.
profiles.refuseToAdmitEarly: Some rooms come back before faces do, and that fact feels safer to him than admitting he sometimes prefers it that way.
profiles.revealMidway: He remembers doors better than people and can describe hinges, floor plans, and sight lines long after the names are gone.
profiles.revealLate: He once moved fast because fear felt better than hesitation, and afterward he kept calling that speed professionalism because the other word was horror.
profiles.collapseMode: Treats the current space like a live breach and misreads the player as threat or teammate, snapping into orders, angles, and exit checks.
profiles.recoveryPath: Slow pacing, orientation to room layout, permission to stop, grounding through touch and distance, and reminders that stillness is not surrender.
